speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, could you describe exactly where the neck pain radiates and which specific fingers on your hand are experiencing the tingling or weakness?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the weakness primarily affect your grip strength or fine motor skills, and does it worsen when you extend your neck or hold your head upright for periods of time? I also need to know if you have any numbness in your saddle area or changes in bladder or bowel function.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text: I need to check for signs of lower motor neuron involvement and rule out other causes. REQUEST TEST: Electromyography_and_Nerve_Conduction_Studies.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the EMG is normal, this rules out peripheral neuropathy and motor neuron disease, pointing strongly to a central cord issue. Given your history of trauma and the specific pattern of hand weakness with preserved leg function, I suspect cervical myelopathy. REQUEST TEST: Cervical_Spinal_MRI

text: Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, hypertension, history of a motor vehicle accident 3 years prior. Social history: 7 sexual partners, uses condoms inconsistently.

speaker: Doctor
text: The social history of inconsistent condom use raises the possibility of an infectious etiology for the syrinx, such as neurosyphilis. I need to rule this out before finalizing the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Syphilis_Serology

speaker: Doctor
text: Since infectious causes like syphilis have been ruled out, the syrinx is likely post-traumatic secondary to your motor vehicle accident. I will now request medical images to better visualize the spinal cord cavity and surrounding structures. REQUEST IMAGES
